overview: Ghana is a country in West Africa, on the Gulf of Guinea. Its capital and largest city is Accra. In 1957 Ghana became the first country in sub-Saharan Africa to win independence from colonial rule, from the United Kingdom. English is the official language, and Ghana is one of the world's biggest producers of cocoa and gold.

geography.text: Ghana is mostly low and gently rolling, with a sandy coastline dotted with lagoons and old European forts. Tropical forest grows in the south-west, and the north is savanna. Lake Volta, created by the Akosombo Dam in the 1960s, is one of the largest artificial lakes in the world by area.

history.text: The Ashanti Empire was a powerful state in the region from around 1700, rich in gold. Europeans built forts along the coast, which they called the Gold Coast, and traded gold and enslaved people. Britain made it a colony in 1874. In 1957 Ghana became the first country in sub-Saharan Africa to win independence from colonial rule, led by Kwame Nkrumah.

events.title: Democracy
events.text: A new constitution brings multi-party elections.

government.text: Ghana is a presidential republic and one of Africa's most stable democracies, with power changing hands peacefully several times. The President is elected for up to two four-year terms.

economy.text: Ghana is Africa's largest gold producer and the world's second-largest cocoa producer. It also exports oil. The economy went through a debt crisis in 2022 and has been recovering.

culture.text: Kente cloth, hand-woven in bright strips, is a symbol of Ghana and listed by UNESCO. Highlife and Afrobeats music, and jollof rice, are part of Ghana's friendly rivalry with Nigeria. Accra's Year of Return in 2019 welcomed people of the African diaspora.

items.title: Cape Coast Castle
items.text: A former slave-trading fort, listed by UNESCO.

items.title: Fantasy coffins
items.text: Coffins shaped like fish, cars or shoes.

sport.text: Football is Ghana's passion. It has won the Africa Cup of Nations four times and reached the World Cup quarter-finals in 2010. Boxing has produced several world champions, such as Azumah Nelson.
